text.p: Strong LME copper spreads kept the market buoyant on Monday afternoon and zinc hovered under fresh seven-year highs ahead of more gains, traders and analysts said.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 1.43 points to 233.61.

On the LME, the three months copper market, which has been virtually ignored recently in favour of cash and the spreads, extended its upward track to hit a high of $2,340 before ending the day $3 firmer at $2,319.
Zinc stocks fell by a healthy 3,650 tonnes, helping prices to power up to hit a fresh peak since August 1990 at $1,540. It finished the kerb $6 firmer at $1,530.
Aluminium also pushed higher, peaking at $1,617 before profit-taking and possible producer activity trimmed gains. Prices ended $1.50 firmer at $1,609.
Nickel held in its $6,700-$6,900 range of the past few days, ending the kerb $50 higher at $6,790.
Tin dipped below $5,420 support to a fresh 2-1/3 year low of $5,400. It ended the day at $5,410, a loss of $50, and traders said more losses were expected.
Lead was little changed at $647 versus $648/49 on Friday and alloy ended at $1,445/50, up slightly from $1,442/45.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on commercial and fund buying tied to a seasonal recovery, traders said. Wheat closed two to 4-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up four at $3.32-1/2. September was up 4-1/4 at $3.40-1/4.

COMEX gold and silver prices ended lower Monday, giving back some of Friday's gains, but NYMEX platinum group metal (PGM) futures ended higher, with Russian supplies still in doubt. COMEX August gold ended down $3.40 at $326.20 an ounce, following a run up to 11 day highs at $330.90 Friday. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted around $325.30/80, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $326.20, and the New York close Friday at $328.70/20.

NYMEX crude settled lower Monday, sagging under losses in gasoline prices and a possible surge in Iraqi oil exports once the oil-for-food deal restarts. "Iraq was definitely a factor today, but the market has been anticipating the Iraqi news for a week or two. Gasoline, however, influenced crude to a larger extent," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston. August crude ended nine cents a barrel off at $19.18. August gasoline settled off 0.01 cent a gallon at 60.04 cents while August heating oil finished 0.13 cent up at 52.35 cents a gallon.
